owned_invariants: A rational is read from an integer or from text of the form p/q: an optional minus, ASCII digits, and optionally a slash and a nonzero denominator in ASCII digits. A plus sign, a space, a decimal point, an exponent, an empty part and a zero denominator are all refused, and so is any value that is not an integer or text.
Every operation is on ratios of unbounded integers in lowest terms. Nothing rounds and nothing overflows.
rref returns the reduced row echelon form and the pivot columns in increasing order. A row shorter than the widest row is read as ending in zeros, so a ragged matrix cannot index out of range.

classify_linear applies the Rouche-Capelli test: inconsistent when rank(A) differs from rank([A|b]), underdetermined when the ranks agree and are below the number of unknowns, and otherwise the one solution, read from the reduced augmented matrix.
polynomial evaluates by Horner's rule with the constant term first; the empty polynomial is zero.
show writes p/q in lowest terms with the sign on p, and writes the denominator even when it is 1.
boundaries: classify_linear takes the number of unknowns from the first row of A and pairs rows with entries of b by position. The caller establishes that A is rectangular and as long as b; wf07.rs does so before calling.

rref and classify_linear index rows and columns directly. Each index is below a length fixed earlier in the same function (rows padded to the width, pivots below the row count, the solution column below the number of unknowns).
Gaussian elimination on unbounded rationals is exact but its numbers can grow; the caller bounds the size of the system.
